chapter: New York arrival, Billy Hicks and the Black Cat
title: Bill Doggett's big band in Philadelphia
summary: Hall describes the arranged ensemble band with Shadow Wilson on drums and how he brought Philadelphia friends to New York.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: That's right, and then prior to that I had been working with Bill Doggett in Philadelphia and we had a big band, Shadow Wilson was the drummer.
Now, when was this. We talked about Philadelphia, but we didn't--
This is just before I left.
Before you went to the Catskills.
Yes.
So you and Bill Doggett had a --
who was the leader of the band.
Bill Doggett. We had a big band. We used to work in ballrooms, but we rehearsed a lot.
This was before he was an organist.
Oh, yes, but we used to play --
Shadows was on drums.
Yeah, we used to play saxophone. What's the --
You mean in those days?
Any days.
Benny Carter.

Benny Carter, we used to play all of his tunes. That type of thing. Bill Doggett was very astute arranger at that period of time, and he reached out far for tunes to play for the band, and we were playing things that were different than anybody else.
Who were your soloists, do you remember.
It wasn't a solo sort of thing, but more an ensemble. I don't remember all the guys in the band. I can find out who they are.
I was just wondering if there was anyone who again like yourself went on to New York and other places.
I left first out of that period. I left
first. Accidentally, and then all the rest of the guys come from Philadelphia, come and look me up. I was known to get them their first gig in New York.
Had to have someone from home to say hello to.
Yeah.
